rubrics.justification: No image-based morphology was assessed, and the response introduced hypothetical blastocyst grades (e.g., 4AA/5AA) not supported by provided visual data.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, BMI, diagnosis, prior biochemical pregnancy, sperm parameters, endometrium, and oocyte yield, though some links to actual embryo quality remain hypothetical.

The reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, clearly separating unavailable image assessment from clinical inference, though the implantation estimate depends on an assumed good-quality embryo.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, including SET in a good-prognosis 33-year-old and cautious use of further testing, though ERA/thrombophilia suggestions are somewhat less guideline-supported unless recurrent failure develops.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, with useful counseling and follow-up suggestions, though some recommendations remain broad rather than highly case-specific.
